phoneticConvention: Approximate respelling for English readers (CAPITALS = stressed syllable; vowels ah / eh / ee / oh / oo; c+e/i → ch, g+e/i → j, gn → ny, gl → ly, sc+e/i → sh, z → ts / dz; double consonants held longer, e.g. kaf-FEH). No substitute for the audio.
reviewStatus: Written by rule from validated content; native English review recommended.
title: My daily life
goal: Describe your daily life, habits and the people around you.

I usually have lunch at home.
I usually take the train.

In my free time I travel.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Hai fratelli o sorelle?
turns.phon: AH-ee frah-TEHL-lee oh soh-REHL-leh
turns.native: Do you have brothers or sisters?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Sì, ho un fratello e una sorella. E tu?
turns.phon: SEE, oh oon frah-TEHL-loh eh OO-nah soh-REHL-lah. eh TOO
turns.native: Yes, I have a brother and a sister. And you?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Io ho due figli.
turns.phon: EE-oh oh DOO-eh FEE-lyee
turns.native: I have two children.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Che bello! Quanti anni hanno?
turns.phon: keh BEHL-loh. KWAHN-tee AHN-nee AHN-noh
turns.native: How nice! How old are they?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Otto e dodici. Abitiamo vicino a Lione.
turns.phon: OHT-toh eh DOH-dee-chee. ah-bee-TYAH-moh vee-CHEE-noh ah LYOH-neh
turns.native: Eight and twelve. We live near Lyon.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: E tua moglie lavora?
turns.phon: eh TOO-ah MOH-lyeh lah-VOH-rah
turns.native: And does your wife work?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Sì, lavora in un ospedale.
turns.phon: SEE, lah-VOH-rah een oon ohs-peh-DAH-leh
turns.native: Yes, she works in a hospital.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Anche mia madre lavora in ospedale!
turns.phon: AHN-keh MEE-ah MAH-dreh lah-VOH-rah een ohs-peh-DAH-leh
turns.native: My mother works in a hospital too!

dialogues.practice: Listen to both roles, hide one role, answer, then swap one line for a variant of your own.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: A che ora ti alzi di solito?
turns.phon: ah keh OH-rah tee AHL-tsee dee SOH-lee-toh
turns.native: What time do you usually get up?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Alle sei e mezza. La mattina porto i bambini a scuola.
turns.phon: AHL-leh SEH-ee eh MEHD-dzah. lah maht-TEE-nah POR-toh ee bahm-BEE-nee ah SKWOH-lah
turns.native: At half past six. In the morning I take the children to school.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: E poi vai al lavoro in macchina?
turns.phon: eh POY VAH-ee ahl lah-VOH-roh een MAHK-kee-nah
turns.native: And then you drive to work?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: No, prendo il treno. E tu?
turns.phon: noh, PREHN-doh eel TREH-noh. eh TOO
turns.native: No, I take the train. And you?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Io lavoro da casa due giorni a settimana.
turns.phon: EE-oh lah-VOH-roh dah KAH-zah DOO-eh JOR-nee ah seht-tee-MAH-nah
turns.native: I work from home two days a week.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Che fortuna! E la sera cosa fai?
turns.phon: keh for-TOO-nah. eh lah SEH-rah KOH-zah FAH-ee
turns.native: Lucky you! And what do you do in the evening?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Spesso vado in palestra, a volte cucino.
turns.phon: SPEHS-soh VAH-doh een pah-LEHS-trah, ah VOHL-teh koo-CHEE-noh
turns.native: I often go to the gym, sometimes I cook.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Io la sera guardo sempre un film.
turns.phon: EE-oh lah SEH-rah GWAR-doh SEHM-preh oon FEELM
turns.native: In the evening I always watch a film.

dialogues.practice: Listen to both roles, hide one role, answer, then swap one line for a variant of your own.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Buongiorno, sono il nuovo vicino. Mi chiamo Paolo.
turns.phon: bwohn-JOR-noh, SOH-noh eel NWOH-voh vee-CHEE-noh. mee KYAH-moh PAH-oh-loh
turns.native: Hello, I'm the new neighbour. My name is Paolo.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Piacere, Anna. Benvenuto! Da dove viene?
turns.phon: pyah-CHEH-reh, AHN-nah. behn-veh-NOO-toh. dah DOH-veh VYEH-neh
turns.native: Nice to meet you, Anna. Welcome! Where are you from?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Sono francese, ma lavoro qui a Bologna.
turns.phon: SOH-noh frahn-CHEH-zeh, mah lah-VOH-roh KWEE ah boh-LOH-nyah
turns.native: I'm French, but I work here in Bologna.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Che lavoro fa?
turns.phon: keh lah-VOH-roh FAH
turns.native: What do you do for a living?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Sono ingegnere, lavoro in una fabbrica.
turns.phon: SOH-noh een-jeh-NYEH-reh, lah-VOH-roh een OO-nah FAHB-bree-kah
turns.native: I'm an engineer, I work in a factory.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Il quartiere Le piace?
turns.phon: eel kwar-TYEH-reh leh PYAH-cheh
turns.native: Do you like the neighbourhood?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Sì, molto. C'è un mercato qui vicino?
turns.phon: SEE, MOHL-toh. cheh oon mehr-KAH-toh KWEE vee-CHEE-noh
turns.native: Yes, a lot. Is there a market nearby?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Sì, ogni sabato mattina, in piazza.
turns.phon: SEE, OH-nyee SAH-bah-toh maht-TEE-nah, een PYAHT-tsah
turns.native: Yes, every Saturday morning, in the square.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Perfetto, grazie!
turns.phon: pehr-FEHT-toh, GRAH-tsyeh
turns.native: Perfect, thanks!

readiness: Describe your habits and your day with frequency words, introduce your family, say where you live and what you do for work or study, and ask the other person the same questions.
